Analysis: Both hypotheses propose that AFP plays an active role in enhancing the IL-6/STAT3 signaling loop in HCC, moving beyond its diagnostic use. However, Hypothesis 1 adds an extra layer by suggesting that STAT3 upregulates AFP to create a bi‐directional positive feedback loop with implications for cancer stem cell formation and immune escape. This additional layer presents a more novel concept but also suffers from added mechanistic uncertainty and complexity that weakens its plausibility and clear testability. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 offers a more streamlined proposition – that AFP actively enhances IL-6/STAT3 signaling – making it somewhat easier to design experiments to validate the proposed interactions. Regarding safety, both hypotheses foresee targeting AFP interactions, yet the simpler mechanism of Hypothesis 2 may allow a more controlled approach with fewer unforeseen effects on competing signaling networks. Overall, the clarity in formulation and potential for focused experiments make Hypothesis 2 superior when considering novelty, plausibility, testability, and safety.
